title: Tutor Intelligence Rents Palletizing Robots for $14 to $18 an Hour
summary:
The Massachusetts-based robotics company is introducing a rental system for its hardware that allows warehouse managers to pay for labor by the hour rather than purchasing equipment upfront. Tutor Intelligence is pricing its palletizing machines between $14 and $18 per hour, which undercuts the $19.35 median hourly wage for manual material movers in the U.S. This pricing model includes support and upgrades without requiring long-term contracts.

The transition to an hourly rental model follows a $75M Series B funding round led by a16z that brings the company's total raised capital to $117M. Tutor employs human teleoperators to direct machines in production environments to build the training data for its robot foundation models. The company has grown its footprint to nearly four times as many sites as a year ago and targets having more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

selectedTweets.text:
We’re thrilled to lead Tutor Intelligence’s Series B.

@tutorintel is a robotics research and deployment company that builds generally capable robot hardware. They deploy into real production environments ahead of full autonomy, using human teleoperators (“tutors”) to train the robot foundation models and make the fleet more capable over time.

To date, Tutor robots are in operation across some of the country’s largest manufacturing and logistics networks, with plans to have more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

Co-founders Josh Gruenstein and Alon Kosowsky are lifelong robotics enthusiasts who met as undergrads at MIT. They combine excellent research chops with a practical, ROI-driven orientation that is more typical in enterprise software.

Congrats @joshgruenstein, @KSachsAlon, and the Tutor Intelligence team!

By @RaghuRaghuram, @martin_casado, and @jamiedsully
